To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a framework where a safe agent modulates a main reward-based reinforcement learning agent to minimize side-effects.
we propose Safety Aware RL (SARL), a framework where a safe agent modulates a main reward-based RL agent to minimize side-effects.

we propose SARL - a framework that learns a task-independent safety policy for a given environment and uses it to modulate the action probabilities of agents solving multiple tasks in that environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of designing agents that learn to minimize their side effects while executing policies in complex environments.
the problem of designing for safety in complex, dynamic environments where agents are expected to execute a primary task while avoiding causing undesired side effects.
designing a reinforcement learning framework that enables agents to safely interact with the real world.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed SARL framework is a generalizable and portable solution to the problem of designing safe agents in complex environments.
our framework provides the benefit of generalizing and porting the learned notion of safety across multiple tasks and policies without the need to re-train the safe agent.
the SARL method provides a framework where a safe agent modulates multiple policies in a given environment to minimize their undesired side effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a framework that can be used for safety aware reinforcement learning.
we propose a framework for safety-aware reinforcement learning, where a safe virtual agent is used to modulate the action probabilities of a reward-seeking main agent.
SARL provides a framework that can be used to modulate multiple reward-based agents to reduce their side effects in a given environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a task-independent notion for safety is sufficient to modulate the behavior of a main agent executing multiple tasks.
a task-agnostic notion of safety can be used to regularize the action probabilities of a reward-based agent, thereby reducing side effects.
a task-independent notion for safety can be learned and used to effectively modulate the actions for agents executing different policies in the same environment.
